title: The scheme theoretic union of two closed subschemes is the pushout of one along their scheme theoretic intersection, and its structure sheaf sits in a short exact sequence
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The claim is that for two closed subschemes X, Y of a scheme S the union X union Y is the pushout of X and Y along their scheme theoretic intersection, and that the structure sheaves fit into 0 -> O_{X union Y} -> O_X x O_Y -> O_{X cap Y} -> 0 (statement lines 558-572). The proof has to do two genuinely different things: construct the four maps of that sequence, including the sign on O_Y -> O_{X cap Y}, and then solve the universal problem for an arbitrary test scheme T. The second part is the non-formal step: the author constructs h : X union Y -> T locally, splitting into the three regions of X union Y, and on the overlap X cap Y reduces the two agreeing morphisms f and g to ring maps B -> A/I and B -> A/J agreeing into A/(I + J), which the exact sequence lifts uniquely to B -> A/(I cap J) (proof lines 596-618). This is H2: a real local construction with a case analysis and an explicit algebraic lift, but no research-level input and no hypothesis beyond the definitions.
